confirmed.description: Marthanda Varma is drawn from Nagoji's bare-headed face studies, not from varma-v1. He has loose, shoulder-length curly black hair with no side knot, a gold drop earring like Nagoji's, and a thick handlebar moustache. Apart from the namam he reads as Nagoji without his turban. The panel border cuts off the top of his head, so no bun shows anywhere. He also does not match himself one page later: in 8.2 and 8.5 his hair is sleek and tied in a bun to his left.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of 7.4 (upper left, figure standing behind Ramayyan): open curly hair falls to his collar, a gold drop hangs at the ear, and the head is cut at the top border. The script asks for 'ONLY the face and moustache from the varma-v1 sheet ... black hair tied in a bun to his left'. CONTINUITY.md says 'bare-headed with his hair in a side knot above his left ear'. In 8.5 the same king has slicked-back hair and a clear bun.

verdict.reason: I'm confirming this. Varma is the standing, bare-chested king behind Ramayyan in the bottom wide panel (7.4). Zoomed in, his black hair hangs in loose curls past both ears to the collar, and his left side (image right) shows no knot or bun. The top border cuts across the crown, so no tie shows anywhere. The script for 7.4 asks for "black hair tied in a bun to his left". CONTINUITY.md says that on the beach he goes bare-headed "with his hair in a side knot above his left ear". The hair also breaks continuity with the next page: in 8.2 (back view) and 8.5 (close-up) the same king has sleek, pulled-back hair with a clear bun. Loose curls like these are the hairstyle of Nagoji's bare-headed studies on nagoji-v2.png, and that sheet is where the "reads as Nagoji" impression comes from. Two parts of the original report are overstated. First, the gold drop earring is allowed, because the varma-v1 face studies show drop earrings too. Second, the namam, gold necklaces, bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth, place under the awning and speech tail still mark him as Varma, so his identity is not lost. The hair is plainly visible at print size, since his head is large in the panel. That makes this a localized error in look and continuity, not a wrong identity: major, not blocker.

confirmed.description: The setting and light both jump. Every other panel in the Kayal scene (10.1, 10.2, 10.4, 10.5) is the palm-lined beach picket line at sunset or dusk. 10.3 puts Nagoji and Kayal in a stone fort courtyard in pale daylight.
confirmed.evidence: 10.3 has crenellated laterite walls on the left, a stone pillar with an iron tether ring on the right, a walled fort on a distant headland, and a pale midday sky. 10.2 just before it shows the sun setting over the sea behind a wooden rail picket line. 10.4 and 10.5 return to the dusk beach with palms and cook fires.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. I zoomed in on page 10, panel 3. On the left there are tall laterite walls with crenellations, and on the right a stone pillar with a big iron tether ring. Lower right there are low fort walls, and a walled fortress sits on a far headland. The sky is pale and hazy with no sunset color, so it reads as midday. Panels 10.1 and 10.2 show the beach picket line at sunset, with wooden rails, palms, cook fires and the sun on the sea. Panels 10.4 and 10.5 go back to the dusk beach. The script leaves no room for this. 9.4 sets the scene as "Dusk. The picket line under the palms". 10.4 calls for "the last light", and 11.1 continues "the last light going blue over the picket line". CONTINUITY.md says Kayal is "chosen at the ch7 picket line" and has no fort or courtyard setting for chapter 7. The panel is the widest one on the page, so the jump in place and time of day is obvious at print size. It is not a blocker: the beat is there, Nagoji and Kayal are correct, the lettering reads fine, and the problem is limited to one panel's background and light. The fix is to redraw the 10.3 background as the dusk beach picket line with warm low light.

confirmed.description: The script has the mixed Madurai and Maravar cavalry line regrouping on the sand. The render shows a large drilled infantry formation that has not appeared in the chapter, with horses in the minority.
confirmed.evidence: Below Varma's shoulder are several ranks of dismounted spearmen in crossed leather belts, many bare-chested in white dhotis and standing at attention (this reads as Travancore regulars). Only about 15 mounted figures stand at the back. The script calls for 'the mixed Madurai and Maravar line regroups on the shining sand'.

verdict.reason: I'm confirming the finding but lowering it to minor. A 3x crop of page 8, panel 2 (page-08.png, about x1150-1690, y580-795 at full resolution) bears out the description. The front of the crowd is several ranks of men on foot standing at attention. They wear white turbans or go bare-headed, some are bare-chested in white lower cloths, and many have crossed leather belts, spears and round shields. There are roughly 60 men on foot against about 13 horses with riders, mostly in the middle and back. That matches neither the cast for this panel (madurai_troop, which the bible describes as white knee-length jamas on tall dark horses) nor the script's 'mixed Madurai and Maravar line regroups'. It also clashes with the next page: in 9.2 the same troop waits at the water fully mounted, with no foot soldiers anywhere. Pages 5.4 and 7.3 also show only riders, so this foot formation appears only here. I'm calling it minor rather than major for three reasons. 8.2 is one of the page's two small top panels, about 2.5 by 1.4 inches in print, and the crowd fills only its lower right. The script asks for 'tiny figures in white turbans and bare heads', and those are there, along with clearly visible horses. Riders resting on foot after the drill is a plausible reading, so the scene still works: the king nods as he looks down at the trainees. The crossed belts and the ratio of foot soldiers to horses are background polish. A redraw should show mostly mounted riders, or riders standing next to their own horses, in white jamas or white mundus, without the drill ranks.

confirmed.description: The king's shelter on the bluff changes form between consecutive panels. 2.2, 8.1 and 8.3 show a plain cloth awning on a wooden pole. 7.4 shows a timber pavilion with several posts, a solid roof and a tall brass standing lamp.
confirmed.evidence: 7.4: thick wooden posts and a roofed eave frame Ramayyan, with a brass nilavilakku on a stand at the far left. 8.1 and 8.3, the very next beats at the same spot, show a single wooden pole holding a cream cloth awning, open on all sides. 8.4 then shows yet another thatched eave over a stone parapet.

verdict.reason:
The finding stands, with one correction. On page 7, panel 4, the zoomed crop of the upper left shows at least four thick, weathered timber posts with cross-beams. Behind them, at the far left, is a plank or woven wall, and a brass nilavilakku stands on a base in front of it. A fifth post stands behind Varma's right side. There is also a stone wall with a wooden fence behind the group. This reads as a walled timber shed. The correction is that the roof is not solid: it is the same cream cloth used elsewhere, so the material matches. The structure does not.

The script for 7.4 says "The top of the bluff, at the one-pole awning". The review notes also list 7.4 among the panels where the one awning must stay the same, so the script does not allow this variation.

On the facing page, 8.1 and 8.3 (crops checked) show a single thin pole holding a cream cloth awning over open, red-earth hillside, with no wall, no lamp and no extra posts. 2.2 also shows a simple cloth awning on poles. Pages 60 and 61 are seen together as a spread, and the posts and wall take up the left third of a half-page panel, so the change is easy to see at print size.

Separately, 8.4 adds a third version, a thatched eave over a stone parapet, which also does not match 8.1 and 8.3. Character identity and the action are correct, so this is a localized set-continuity error, not a blocker. The fix is to redraw the 7.4 background as the one-pole cloth awning, and to align 8.4 to it as well.

confirmed.description: The lighting and setting break from the scene around it. 7.1 continues the crouched talk from 6.5 (bright midday), and 7.2 is also bright midday, but 7.1 is lit as a golden sunset. A stone fortress also appears on the headland, where pages 1 to 6 show only a palm-crowned laterite bluff. The sand map is redrawn as loose loops with no straight Dutch line.
confirmed.evidence: 7.1 has a low sun, orange-pink clouds and glinting surf, and a crenellated stone fort on the rocky headland at the top right. 6.5 and 7.2 have flat blue noon skies and no fort. Raza Khan's finger traces a looping curve, while 6.5 shows a straight groove with an arc on each side.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 7, panel 1. The lighting does not match the panels around it. 7.1 is lit as golden hour: an orange and pink sky with lit clouds at upper left, and sun glints on the surf and wet sand at lower left. The panel before it (6.5) has a flat blue noon sky, and so does the panel after it (7.2). The script makes 7.1 a direct continuation of the 6.5 crouch: Raza Khan is "still crouched" and the dialogue picks up where 6.5 left off. The first sign of time passing is in 7.3 ("Afternoon, the sun lower"), and even that is not sunset. At this size, a warm low-sun palette between two blue noon panels reads as a time jump that the story does not have.

The fort is also there. A crop of the top right shows crenellated stone walls and towers on a rocky headland behind Raza Khan's turban. The script, the bible and the visible backgrounds of pages 1 to 6 (also checked at small size on 8 and 9) show only the palm-crowned laterite bluff, and nothing calls for a fort. A similar small fort with a red flag also appears in the background of 7.4, which is a separate but related landmark inconsistency.

The sand-map part of the claim is weak. The script calls it "the half-erased map", and the crop still shows a diagonal central groove with a loop on each side. That is a loose but readable version of the 6.5 drawing and is not a problem on its own. Even so, the lighting break and the unexplained fort are clear, localized continuity errors that need this one panel regenerated. That fits major rather than blocker: identity, lettering and story beats are all correct.

confirmed.description: The chapter's payoff panel is lost. The script asks for a wide, half-page panel of the mixed line wheeling in one clean turn with the riders sitting quiet. Instead it is a small half-width box in the middle tier, and its two narration captions fill the top half. The captions sit exactly where the riders' torsos and heads are, so the line reads as riderless horses splashing along. Only the far-right rider shows.
confirmed.evidence: Page 7, middle tier, right box: both captions ('Men began to trust...' and 'Horses began to trust...') reach from the top border down to the horses' backs. Below them you see only horse bodies and legs, no white turbans and no bare-headed Maravar. The panel is about a quarter of the page, not half.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 7 (/Users/roshanvenugopal/Documents/github/nagoji/output/comic-v15-full-redo/chapters/ch07/renders/r5/page-07.png), panel 7.3, but the right severity is major, not blocker. The script calls for a wide panel taking half the page. The render puts 7.3 in the right half of the middle tier, which is about an eighth of the page. A zoomed crop shows both caption boxes running from the top border down to the horses' backs. Every rider's head and torso is covered except the far-right white-turbaned rider with the lance. No bare-headed Maravar is visible, and the line reads as horses splashing through surf with only legs and saddles showing. So the 'mixed line, riders sitting quiet, one clean turn' beat does not come through on the printed page. The reason it is major rather than blocker: the selected art in chapters/ch07/frames/page-07-panel-03-v03.png already contains the full beat. It shows a gently curving line that alternates white-turbaned riders on dark horses with bare-headed Maravar on dun ponies, all sitting quiet in heavy spray. The beat is lost only through panel size, crop and caption placement, which matches the rubric's 'awkward crop hiding the action' (major). Fixing it means re-laying out the page, not redrawing: give 7.3 a full-width half-page tier and move the captions into the open sky on the right of the frame. It should be fixed before publication because it is the chapter's payoff panel.

confirmed.description: The tender close two-shot is mostly covered by lettering, and the 'Kayal.' tail points at the horse. The 'Kayal.' tail ends in the mare's forelock between her ears, not at Nagoji, so the name looks as if it comes from or belongs to the horse. The 9-line narrow balloon 'You will learn the sand...' covers almost all of Kayal's face; only one eye shows. The caption 'The word came unbidden...' sits on top of Nagoji's rust-red turban.
confirmed.evidence: Page 10, bottom-left panel: the 'Kayal.' balloon at the top centre has its tail tip on the mare's poll. The tall balloon on the right half hides her face, muzzle and the last light on her coat. The caption box's lower edge cuts across the top of the turban.

verdict.reason: Partly confirmed: the speaker tail is wrong, but most of the coverage complaint does not hold. On page 10, panel 10.4 (bottom left), the tail of the "Kayal." balloon runs down and to the left and ends in the mare's black mane just behind her ears. Nagoji's turban and mouth are well to the left of that point, so the tail clearly points at the horse's head, not at him. Because his mouth is hidden against her face, a reader could take the name as coming from the horse. A wrong speaker tail counts as major. It is a localized fix: re-aim the tail down and left toward Nagoji's mouth or face. The other two claims are overstated. The tall "You will learn the sand..." balloon covers the right side of Kayal's cheek and jaw, but her eye, forehead, noseband, muzzle and nostril still show at the left, and Nagoji's face, moustache, ear stud and the hand on her muzzle are all clear, so the tender two-shot still reads. The caption box covering the top of the turban is allowed: the script asks only for "rust-red turban edge in frame", and part of the turban still shows. Those two points are minor polish at most. The tail error sets the severity at major.

confirmed.description: The words no rider spoke are lettered as plain narration. The script and the selection manifest both mark this caption as italic. It renders in the same upright face and box as Nagoji's narration, so it reads as Nagoji's own voice, and the setup for Ponnan saying 'Deccan man' aloud in 4.3 is lost.
confirmed.evidence: Page 1, panel 1.3 (horse's eye): the lower caption 'You do not belong here, Deccan man.' is upright condensed sans in a white box, the same as 'Every rolling eye said...' above it. SELECTION-MANIFEST-r5.json carries the speaker as 'CAPTION (italic...'.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 1, panel 1.3. Cropped at full resolution, the lower caption "You do not belong here, Deccan man." uses the same upright condensed DIN face and plain white box as "Every rolling eye said what the riders did not dare speak aloud." above it. There is no oblique. Script line 32 of CHAPTER-07-SCRIPT.md asks for "CAPTION (italic, the words no rider spoke)". The cause is in SELECTION-MANIFEST-r5.json line 52: the text has no paired asterisks. The compositor only sets italics from `*...*` markers (pipeline/README.md, around line 93), so the "italic" in the speaker label has no effect. Chapter 6's italic captions carry the markers and do render in italic. So this is a real deviation from the script and from the book's own convention for unspoken voice, and it is a one-line fix. I rate it minor, not major. The caption directly above says the riders' eyes spoke what they did not say aloud, so readers will take the line as that unspoken thought, not as Nagoji's narration. The words are correct and easy to read, and the echo of "Deccan man" in 4.3 still works because the words match. The reviewer's claim that the setup is "lost" goes too far. The missing italic is a polish issue, not a broken beat.

confirmed.description: The reading order breaks the exchange. Ramayyan's reply 'Voices matter. Especially when the sea is loud.' is stacked against his first balloon, at the same height as Nagoji's 'They obeyed the king's order. I am only the voice today.' The two Ramayyan balloons read as one run, so 'Voices matter' is likely read before the 'only the voice' line it answers. That balloon also covers the back half of Ramayyan's head, and its tail stabs into his eye.
confirmed.evidence: Page 8, large middle panel: Nagoji's balloon top is at y of about 887 and Ramayyan's second balloon top at about 878 (1325-wide view), side by side. The second Ramayyan balloon butts against the first one's tail and overlaps the right side of his skull.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 8, panel 8.3. The script's order is Ramayyan "They obeyed you...", then Nagoji "They obeyed the king's order. I am only the voice today.", then Ramayyan "Voices matter. Especially when the sea is loud." I measured pixel columns at x = 900, 1000 and 1100 in the 1325-wide view. Ramayyan's first balloon ends at y 870 to 872, and his second balloon starts at y 877 to 879. That leaves a gap of about 5 display px, roughly 0.6 mm at 300 DPI, so the two balloons look joined, which readers take to mean one speaker continuing. The second balloon also butts against the first balloon's tail. Its text line sits at about y 917 to 929, which is level with or above Nagoji's first text line, while Nagoji's balloon is far left and a little lower (top at about y 887). So a reader goes from Ramayyan's first balloon straight down into "Voices matter" before reaching the "only the voice" line it answers, and the exchange reads out of order. The other points also check out but matter less. The second Ramayyan balloon covers the back of his bald crown and hair, though his face and ear stay readable. Its tail tip lands on his cheek at the outer corner of his eye, and the first balloon's tail also ends at his other brow, so both tails cut into his face. Only the lettering is wrong, and moving the balloons fixes it without redrawing the art (for example, put Nagoji's balloon high on the left and the second Ramayyan balloon lower on the right, and stop the tails short of his face). That makes it major rather than blocker.

confirmed.description: The off-panel tail for Nagoji's Dutch-square line points the wrong way. Nagoji is in 3.1 to the left, but the tail runs right, across the sky and over the awning where the king and Ramayyan sit, to the right border. This invites reading the line as the king's. The balloon is also a cramped 10-line column of one to three words per line, and its edge overlaps the back of Raza Khan's turban.
confirmed.evidence: Page 3, top-right panel: the balloon 'If you charge a Dutch square...' runs from the top border down to y of about 630, with the tail exiting toward the right border at y of about 335, just above the awning figures.

verdict.reason: The art shows the problem. In panel 3.2 the off-panel tail for 'If you charge a Dutch square...' leaves the balloon's right side at about y 270 to 400 in the 1838px original. It runs right across the open sky and ends at the right panel border at about (1675, 465), just above the awning where the king and Ramayyan sit, who are the only other figures in the panel. The script marks this line NAGOJI (off). Nagoji is in 3.1 to the left, facing right, and Raza Khan's head is turned left toward him. So an off-panel tail should point left. This one points right, toward where Raza's eyes flick, at the king. The caption 'The king had set a stranger over him.' sits directly under the awning, which makes the line even easier to read as the king's. The tail is large and plain at print size, so this is not too slight to matter. It is a wrong-direction speaker tail, which the rubric names as major: clearly wrong but limited to one panel, and the panel's text is still readable. The other points are true but small. The balloon is a narrow 10-line column of one to three words per line, and its left edge covers the back of Raza's turban. Both are polish (minor), and neither makes the lettering unreadable. The fix is to re-letter 3.2 with the off-panel tail exiting toward the left border, or toward the gutter shared with 3.1, and to widen the balloon.

confirmed.description: The crop and the balloons hide Raza Khan's identity marker and crowd his face. His forehead and deep-green turban are cut off by the panel's top border, so the frown the script asks for is cut. The two balloons press in on both sides of his face; the right one covers the back of his head and ear.
confirmed.evidence: Page 2, bottom panel: only a sliver of green turban shows above his eyes at the top border. The 'My men ride to break lines...' balloon's left edge overlaps his ear and hair; the left balloon's tail touches his moustache.

verdict.reason: I confirmed the problem, but it is minor, not major. In the zoomed crop of page 2, panel 2.5, the top panel border cuts across Raza Khan's head just above his eyebrows. Only a strip of dark-green turban about 20 px high (roughly 1.7 mm in print) is left. The script asks for a "deep-green high-wrapped turban", and the bible says the green turban is what sets him apart from his white-turbaned troop, so the head crop is a real composition fault. The right balloon ("My men ride to break lines...") also covers his ear and the grey hair behind it. With the two balloons on either side, his face is boxed in. One detail of the report is overstated: the left balloon's tail stops just short of his moustache and does not touch it. It is still not major because he stays easy to identify and the beat still works. The scar on his left cheek reads clearly, as do the pointed moustache and the green cloth over his shoulder, and panel 2.4 above shows him in full in the green turban. His lowered brow is still visible under the border, so the frown reads, and no balloon covers his eyes, mouth or scar. Fix: lower the figure, or redraw with headroom so the turban shows, and pull the right balloon off the back of his head.

confirmed.description: A 12-line, two-to-three-words-per-line column balloon hides the panel's action. The script has Nagoji's hand still on Kayal's black mane. The balloon covers Kayal's head and neck and most of his reaching arm, so only his fingertips on the mane show. The column itself is awkward to read.
confirmed.evidence: Page 11, third tier, right panel: the balloon 'I pray to whatever is listening...' runs from the top border to the bottom of the panel at x of about 765 to 960 (1325-wide view), over the mare's head. Only a hand and a strip of mane show at its upper-left edge.

verdict.reason: I checked the original 1838x2775 render and zoomed in on panel 11.4. The problem is real. The balloon "I pray to whatever is listening..." is a narrow column of 12 lines with 2 or 3 words per line. It runs from the top border of the panel almost to the bottom, at roughly x 1060 to 1335 in the original image. It covers all of Kayal's head and upper neck, and all of Nagoji's right arm from shoulder to wrist. All that shows of the scripted beat ("one hand still on Kayal's black mane") is three fingertips coming out from behind the balloon's upper-left edge onto a strip of black mane. Because the arm is hidden, the hand looks disconnected from Nagoji, and the mare reads as a headless body at the left edge. Nothing in the script or the bible allows the mare's head or Nagoji's touch to be hidden here. The column shape is also awkward to read, though every line is legible. A large area of empty sunset sky to the upper right of Nagoji's head could take a wider, shorter balloon. Severity: major, not blocker. The beat is technically present (fingers on mane), the lettering is readable, and the problem is limited to this one panel. It fits "awkward crop hiding the action" and can be fixed by moving and reshaping the balloon, without redrawing the art.

confirmed.description: The chapter's closing image is shrunk and buried. The script asks for 12.4 and 12.5 at full width, with 12.5 the largest panel on the page. Both render half-width, and 12.5 is shorter than 12.4 beside it, with mismatched top and bottom edges. Three stacked captions cover most of Kayal's body and forelegs. The last caption, scripted as 'separate, weighted', looks like the others.
confirmed.evidence: Page 12, bottom-right panel: 'Storms did not ask permission.' covers Kayal's barrel and shoulder, and 'Perhaps horses, taught well, did not either.' covers her forelegs next to the hoofprints. Nagoji is clipped at the right border. Its top edge is about 27px lower and its bottom about 25px higher than 12.4's (1325-wide view).

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 12, panel 12.5. Both the current script and the render-time SCRIPT-SOURCE.md say 12.5 should be "Full width, bottom, the largest panel on the page". In the render it shares the bottom row with 12.4 at half width. On the 1838x2775 PNG its borders run from y=1935 to y=2503 (about 568px tall). 12.4 next to it runs from y=1897 to y=2541 (about 644px), so 12.5 starts about 38px lower and ends about 38px higher. That is about 3mm at 300 DPI, enough to see in print. 12.5 is also much smaller than the full-width 12.1. LAYOUT-solved-s5c.json shows why: the solver relaxed page 12's "size floors and solo" cues to keep page fill at or above 0.75. That was a pipeline compromise. Nothing in the script or the bible allows it. In the zoomed crop, "Storms did not ask permission." covers Kayal's shoulder and barrel, and "Perhaps horses, taught well, did not either." covers her forelegs, right beside the water-filled hoofprints. Only her head, neck, saddle, hindquarters and hooves show. The final caption, scripted "separate, weighted", is a plain box in the same style and size as the other two. Nagoji's right elbow and back touch the right border; that part is minor. The beat itself is still there (Nagoji alone with Kayal at night, hoofprints filling, sea behind), so this is not a missing beat or a blocker. It is a localized layout and lettering failure on the chapter's closing image: major.

confirmed.description: The page's emphasis is inverted. 2.1 (Ponnan's first appearance) and 2.2 (the king and Ramayyan) are squeezed into a short top tier where tall captions cover about half of each image. The scripted tight insert 2.3 (the brand) gets the biggest panel on the page. In 2.1 the second caption covers the Maravar riders behind Ponnan and cuts through the second rider. In 2.2 Varma and Ramayyan are thumbnail-sized.
confirmed.evidence: Page 2, top tier, about 210px tall at 1325-wide view. 'He had already ridden the inland tracks...' runs from the top to the bottom border at the right of 2.1, over the second Maravar. 'Marthanda Varma had told me...' covers the left 40% of 2.2. The 2.3 forearm insert fills about 520px of height.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute this. The art and the layout data both show the problem.

1. **Row heights.** LAYOUT-solved-s5c.json sets page 2 to [[70.8, 70.8], 171.6, 146.2, 128.9]. The top tier holding 2.1 and 2.2 is 70.8pt, about 1 inch at print. Panel 2.3, scripted as "Insert, tight", is 171.6pt and is the tallest panel on the page. The page 2 script gives no size cue that would call for this.

2. **Panel 2.1.** At native resolution the two caption boxes cover about 52% of the panel area. The first runs from the left edge to about 29% of the width and down about 70% of the height. The second runs the full height of the right third.
   - The source frame (frames/page-02-panel-01-v01.png) shows Ponnan in a line of about six Maravar riders on a rocky bluff.
   - In the render, the strip crop removes the bluff entirely, so the scripted "low angle up at the bluff" is lost and Ponnan is cut off at the knee.
   - The left caption hides the left two riders except for their horses' legs. The right caption clips the visible right rider's horse and hides the far-right rider.
   - The result is Ponnan plus one rider and some fragments, which weakens the scripted "line of Maravar horsemen".
   - This is Ponnan's first appearance. The chapter 6 script says he is introduced as leader in chapter 7, and the name caption confirms it.
   - The reviewer's "cuts through the second rider" is slightly overstated: that rider's face and body are visible, and only his horse's head is clipped.

3. **Panel 2.2.** The caption covers the left 40% of the width, nearly full height (about 34% of the area). The tiny size of Varma and Ramayyan is NOT a defect on its own. The script asks for a long shot of "two small figures", so that part of the claim is refuted.

**Severity:** major rather than blocker. All beats are present, the lettering is readable, and Ponnan is recognisable. The damage is a localized layout and crop problem that hides the action and the setting. It can be fixed by re-solving page 2's row heights (taller top tier, smaller 2.3) from the existing frames, without a redraw.

confirmed.description: The page-6 layout does not follow the script and the grid looks broken. The overhead insets 6.3 and 6.4 should sit side by side in the upper sea-and-sky band of 6.5. They render as a separate tier with a wide cream gap between them, and 6.4 stops well short of the right margin, leaving a cream hole. Panel widths on this page take five different values.
confirmed.evidence: Page 6, third tier: 6.3 runs from x of about 108 to 660 and 6.4 from about 733 to 1148 (1325-wide view), against the 1217 right margin, so the gutter between them is about 73px against the usual 6 to 8px. 6.5 below has no insets.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. I measured the panel borders on the full 1838x2775 render. On page 6, 6.3 runs from x 148 to 915 and 6.4 from x 1016 to 1594, both on a separate tier (y 1423 to 1765) between 6.2 and 6.5. That leaves a 101px cream gutter between them, about 0.34 in at 300 DPI, where the chapter's usual gutter is 6px. 6.4 is centred in its half-slot (921 to 1688), so a 94px cream hole sits at the right margin. 6.5 below (148 to 1688) has no insets. minors.description: The script marks Raza Khan's line as a small balloon, almost to himself, but it is lettered at full size like every other balloon.
minors.evidence: Page 7, middle-left panel: 'If the horses hold.' uses the same point size and balloon weight as 'Make them hold.'

minors.description: The 'separate, weighted' caption 'Anticipation.' is a small standard caption tucked in a corner. The scripted narrow eye strip renders as a tall panel whose right half is empty dark background.
minors.evidence: Page 9, third tier: a small caption box at the top right, about 140 by 65px at 1325-wide view. The panel is about 360px tall, not a strip.

minors.description: Two of the scripted wides, 8.2 (over Varma's shoulder) and 8.4 (open sea with Varma), render as small quarter-page panels. The dialogue two-shot 8.3 takes about half the page, so the wides no longer break up the faces as the script intends.
minors.evidence: Page 8: 8.2 is the top-right quarter box and 8.4 the bottom-left quarter box. 8.3 spans full width from y of about 580 to 1450 (1325-wide view).

minors.description: Captions are set flush against the panel borders instead of inset, as they are in the approved Chapter 1. This recurs through the chapter, for example 1.1, 1.2, 1.4, 1.5, 2.1, 4.1, 9.5, 10.1, 10.3, 10.5 and 11.1.
minors.evidence: Page 1: the 1.1 caption's top edge merges with the panel's top border, and the 1.4 caption is jammed into the top-left corner. Ch01 r6 page 1 captions sit about 15px inside the border.

minors.description: Two caption boxes cover about 60% of this small panel, so the 'line of Maravar horsemen' on the bluff is reduced to fragments and the low angle up at the bluff does not read. Ponnan alone carries the panel.
minors.evidence: page-02.png, top-left panel: the 'Ponnam Pandya Deven...' box covers the left third and the 'He had already ridden...' box covers the right third. Only Ponnan and one rider behind him are fully visible.

minors.description: The script asks for the unspoken words to be set in an italic caption, to set them apart from Nagoji's narration. They are set in the same roman caption style as the narration box above, so 'You do not belong here, Deccan man' can be read as Nagoji speaking.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, middle-right panel: the lower box 'You do not belong here, Deccan man.' uses the same upright font and box as 'Every rolling eye said...'.

minors.description: The salute beat is missing: Raza Khan grips his lance upright at mid-shaft instead of saluting with the spear butt to his chest. The tail of his second balloon, 'We have fought for Madurai...', points toward the white-turbaned rider and horse at his right (our left), not clearly at Raza.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, lower-left panel: his right hand holds the lance shaft at chest height with the butt below the frame. The lower-left balloon's tail ends near the horse head at about x=265, y=1590 (display scale).

minors.description: The page layout differs from the script. Panels 6.3 and 6.4 should be square insets placed side by side in the upper band of 6.5, over open sea and sky, with 6.5 filling the lower half. Instead they are wide rectangles in their own tier, and 6.5 takes only about a third of the page. All five beats are still present.
minors.evidence: page-06.png: tier 3 holds two separate wide panels with a gutter between them. Panel 6.5 sits below them as its own frame.

minors.description: Continuity breaks from 6.5. The 'half-erased map' is a loop with a cross-stroke, unlike the straight line with two curves drawn in 6.5. The sky is golden sunset, although 7.1 continues the midday scene and 7.2 and 7.3 are in afternoon daylight. An unscripted European-looking stone castle stands on the headland, and similar forts recur in 7.4, 9.2 and 10.3, though the script's beach is set between a palm-crowned laterite bluff and the sea.
minors.evidence: page-07.png, top panel: an oval loop with a diagonal line in the sand under Raza's finger, an orange sunset sky, and a crenellated fortress at the top right.

minors.description: The script's one-pole cloth awning has become a multi-post wooden pavilion with a writing table, pot and stacked palm-leaf bundles, which does not match 2.2 and 3.2. The top of Varma's head is cropped, so the bun to his left does not read.
minors.evidence: page-07.png, bottom panel: at least three wooden posts and a cloth roof, a heavy table in the foreground, and Varma's hair cut off by the top border.

minors.description: Kayal is not watching Nagoji come. She looks out of the panel to the right and toward the reader, while he approaches from the left in 9.4 and 10.1. She also wears a quilted saddle on the picket line, where the script has the horses rubbed down for the night, and she stays saddled through pages 10 to 12.
minors.evidence: page-09.png, lower-right panel: her head is turned to the right and a saddle pad sits on her back. The saddle pad recurs in 10.3, 10.5, 11.1, 11.2 and 12.5.

minors.description: The script marks the 'Anticipation.' caption as 'separate, weighted', but it is set in a plain small box like every other caption, so the beat lacks the emphasis it asks for.
minors.evidence: page-09.png, third tier: a small plain 'Anticipation.' box in the top-right corner, in the standard caption font and weight.
